question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the mandatory requirements for Video In-Person Verification (VIPV)?

answer.text: A live VIPV with the client clearly recognizable and uncovered, a random question/response for liveness, and secure date/time-stamped saving of the recording
A pre-recorded video submitted later by the client is sufficient
The client may partially cover their face for privacy during VIPV
The video can be recorded at any convenient time and submitted at a later date

explanation.text: The Logic: VIPV requirements include conducting the verification in a live environment with the client clearly recognizable and not covering their face, using a random question and response to confirm the session is not pre-recorded, matching the client with the Aadhaar photo, and digitally saving the recording with a secure, tamper-proof date and time stamp. The Trap: Pre-recorded submissions, partial face covering, and delayed uploads all break the live-verification and liveness-check requirements built into VIPV. Each of the wrong options describes a workflow that the rule explicitly rejects. Note: Rewrote the correct option as a standalone enumerated requirement list (no "All of the above") so it remains correct under answer randomization, and removed the cross-exam and pro-tip paragraphs.
